The codebase is deliberately lightly annotated: models carry full field
definitions, services carry docstrings explaining which feature ID they
implement, and view functions take a plain `request`. Adding parameter
annotations to every view is churn with no safety benefit, because Django
already enforces the request/response contract at runtime.
That choice means Pylance cannot infer Django's dynamic types, so it emits
several hundred 'partially unknown' diagnostics on correct code. Those are
The rules that DO catch real bugs stay on: unused imports, optional member
access on a possibly-None value, undefined names, and argument type
errors. An unused import or a None dereference is a bug worth a red squiggle.
